1.note: Printed 'book 12, chapter 6'; the story of Joḥanan, Jeshua and Bagoas is Antiquities 11.7.1. Kept as printed.

2.note: Printed 'book 12, chapter 2'; Alexander's visit to Jerusalem is Antiquities 11.8.4-6. Kept as printed.

3.note: The priest called 'messenger of the Lord' is Malachi 2:7; reference kept as printed.

4.note: The exegesis of 'thus' (koh) stands in Sifre Numbers §39 in the usual editions; kept as printed.

5.he: אשר זמן חבורה באגרת שנית מאוחר מאד
5.note: Elliptic; "the second letter" refers to Esther 9:29 ("this second letter of Purim"). Read: its composition, including the second letter, is very late.

6.note: Printed so; the mishnah "All the Holy Writings may be rescued from a fire" is Shabbat 16:1.

7.note: Weiss's name for Josephus (Flavius Josephus); the reference is to Against Apion.

8.note: Printed so; the phrase is odd. Read as "established (fixed) matters", i.e. decisions that stood.

9.note: Literal; the sense seems to be that he is taken from the altar for execution, not merely for trial.

10.note: Abbreviation printed thus; most likely Zunz, Gottesdienstliche Vorträge.

11.note: Printed so; read as "satisfy themselves with".

12.note: A letter is broken in the print; read בררנו, "as we have made clear".

13.note: The print is damaged here (it looks like "הרב רבו אהד; יעלליגעק"); the reading as Adolf (Aaron) Jellinek is a conjecture.

14.note: 5625 = 1864/65, as printed; Weiss's Sifra edition is usually dated Vienna 1862 (תרכ"ב).

15.note: Print unclear (OCR ח"ר); read as ח"ד, vol. 4.
